text.tspan: ECS IAM roles: instance profile (agent), task execution role, task role (app)
used by the agent for each task
solid = course slide · dashed = docs: on Fargate there is no instance profile, so the task execution role does the image pulls, logs and secrets
Docs: there are THREE roles, not two
Course: the instance profile (EC2 launch type only) is used by the ECS agent to call the ECS API, send container logs to CloudWatch Logs, pull images
from ECR and read secrets from Secrets Manager / SSM Parameter Store. The task role gives each task its own permissions.
1. Container instance role (instance profile, ecsInstanceRole, AmazonEC2ContainerServiceforEC2Role): lets the ECS agent and Docker daemon call AWS APIs.
EC2 and external (Anywhere) instances only. Never Fargate.
2. Task EXECUTION role (ecsTaskExecutionRole, AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy): used by the ECS / Fargate agent to PULL images from private ECR,
SEND logs to CloudWatch Logs (awslogs) and FETCH secrets (Secrets Manager / SSM Parameter Store) for the task. Containers can't use it.
3. Task role (in the task definition; trust ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com): permissions for YOUR APP code (S3, DynamoDB...). Credentials from
169.254.170.2, rotated, valid 6 h by default. One role per task definition / service = least privilege.
Exam: "container can't read the S3 bucket" → fix the TASK role. "Task fails: can't pull image / can't fetch secret" → fix the task EXECUTION role.
